handdraw-simple.promptBase: Create a clean hand-drawn infographic in a simple sketched style. Use a white or off-white background, neat black hand-drawn outlines, slightly imperfect but controlled linework, plenty of negative space and a large readable title. Make the main chart or map the focus. Use few labels and at most two or three short handwritten arrows or notes. An optional simple character may appear on one side only if useful. Prioritize exact data and quick reading. Avoid clutter, tiny details, heavy textures, many characters, speech bubbles and complex scenes.

micro-people-data.promptBase: Create a hand-drawn illustrated infographic map where tiny cartoon people embody data. Use black hand-drawn outlines, an off-white background, tiny readable round-headed figures and organized groups distributed in the relevant regions. Groups must represent concentration, activity, behavior, community or human presence described in the supplied evidence. Add only useful small icons, a clear title area and a few short annotations. Keep geographic regions recognizable. Avoid chaotic crowds, unreadable microdetails, random decorative people and excessive speech bubbles. Unless an exact pictogram scale is explicitly supplied, people are qualitative metaphors, not countable statistical units: state this visibly in the artwork.

editorial-data.promptBase: Create a polished editorial data infographic in a clean, modern, highly visual card layout. Prioritize data communication: a strong central map, chart or diagram, bold readable title, explanatory subtitle, clear legends, precise labels and concise callouts. Use solid well-defined category colors or honest intensity gradients. Add metric boxes, a ranked list or a supporting data panel only when supplied data makes them useful. Top: title and subtitle. Center: main map or chart. Side or lower area: supporting legend, ranking or metrics. Bottom: exact source line and small WWMaps branding. Use flat or lightly textured off-white background, balanced alignment, generous spacing and high contrast. Optional small icons may clarify the data. Avoid narrative scenes, decorative crowds, excessive illustration, speech bubbles, clutter, tiny text and visual confusion between categories or values. The result must read as an organized statistical infographic that can be scanned in seconds.
